summary: At just 3.9 square miles, Lemon Grove is one of the smallest incorporated cities in San Diego County, yet it packs nearly 28,000 people into that footprint at a density north of 7,100 per square mile — tighter than many neighborhoods in the city of San Diego itself. The terrain rolls through the inland mesa-and-canyon landscape east of downtown San Diego, where modest mid-century homes line hilly streets that occasionally open to long eastward views of the foothills leading toward the Laguna Mountains. This is firmly a bedroom community: most employment draws from the broader San Diego economy — healthcare systems, defense contractors, and the military installations clustered around the region — and the commute into central San Diego runs roughly 15 minutes west on state routes 94 and 125. A home-price-to-income ratio above eight means that at the median household income of about $79,300, purchasing at the median $640,600 is a serious stretch, while median rent of $1,769 consumes roughly 27 percent of gross monthly income, landing in a range that's tight but not crushing. Daily highs averaging 72°F year-round with 9.5 hours of sunshine deliver classic inland San Diego weather — warmer and drier than the coast, cooler than the deep inland valleys. The retail corridor along Broadway carries a mix of taco shops, pho restaurants, and fast-casual chains that signals a functional commercial strip rather than a destination dining scene, and a weekend farmers' market adds fresh-produce access. Lemon Grove reads less as a place with a carefully cultivated identity and more as an affordable pressure valve for a region where even modest housing costs keep climbing.
